title: Shift planning and service-level scope
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Trainee or new worker on the solar panel cleaning track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Explain and demonstrate shift planning and service-level scope

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the solar panel cleaning track. Panels are usually mounted on roofs or elevated structures and are connected to DC and AC electrical circuits. Panels can produce voltage in daylight even when the rest of the system is off. Cleaning on this track does not include electrical work, isolation of the system, opening enclosures, or cable or connector repair. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body:
Learning outcome
By the end of this lesson, demonstrate the ability to translate a service schedule into a workable shift while respecting the approved service plan, site procedures and limits of the cleaning role.

Workplace procedure
Read the signed scope and site-specific schedule: areas, frequency, timing, service standard, exclusions, chemicals permitted and required records. Separate daily high-touch work from periodic tasks and special requests. Sequence work around occupancy, access restrictions and drying time. Allocate staff according to competency and available hours, allowing time for inspections and waste transfer. Escalate any conflict between the schedule and safe completion; do not silently omit work.

Decision boundaries
Before acting, confirm authorisation, hazards and the person responsible for escalation. If the task exceeds training, consent, safe access or agreed scope, pause the affected work, protect others as appropriate, report promptly and document the reason. Never substitute an improvised method for a required specialist procedure.

Worked workplace example
A client asks for a deep carpet extraction during a routine evening clean. The shift lead records the request as outside scope and seeks approval and suitable trained operators rather than adding it without authority.

Guided practical exercise
Given a three-hour office schedule and a list of 15 tasks, create a timed route, identify two infeasible tasks and draft a clear scope-clarification message.

Assessment and feedback
An assessor should observe a complete demonstration and confirm: Creates a realistic prioritised plan, preserves contracted scope and flags capacity or access conflicts early. If a critical safety, privacy or consent step is missed, provide targeted feedback and require reassessment before signoff.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Read the signed scope and site schedule for areas, frequency, timing, service standard, exclusions, permitted chemicals and required records.
Separate daily high-touch work from periodic tasks and special requests.
Sequence work around occupancy, access restrictions and drying time.
Allocate staff by competency and available hours, allowing time for inspections and waste transfer.
Build a timed route for the shift in the order the sequence requires.
Flag any task that does not fit the time, access or competency available, and any capacity or access conflict, as early as possible.
Record out-of-scope requests and obtain approval before adding them to the shift.
Escalate any conflict between the schedule and safe completion, and do not silently omit work.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

summary: The signed scope and site schedule are read, with daily high-touch work separated from periodic tasks and special requests.
Work is sequenced around occupancy, access restrictions and drying time, and staff are allocated by competency and available hours.
Any conflict between the schedule and safe completion is escalated, and no work is silently omitted.

knowledgeChecks.question: What observable actions demonstrate that you can translate a service schedule into a workable shift?
options: Adding every requested task to the shift without checking the time and the travel between rooms
A timed route that separates daily and periodic tasks, with any tasks that do not fit flagged
Dropping the longest tasks without telling anyone and skipping the daily work
Starting with the room the worker likes best, to keep morale up and leaving the hardest room for last

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do when the signed scope for a shift conflicts with what is on site?
options: Skip the unclear task and say nothing and carry on with the next room quietly
Complete the unclear task in the way the worker finds easiest and report it at the end
Pause the affected part, escalate the conflict, and do not silently omit contracted work
Ask the client to decide everything while you keep working and do the tasks in any order

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say to separate when building a shift?
options: Daily high-touch work from periodic tasks and special requests
